digest.component_or_area: LLM provider layer - Bedrock native integration
propositions: rebar requires a first-class native Bedrock provider (BedrockConverseModel) as an alternative to fronting Bedrock with an OpenAI-compatible gateway, to preserve prompt caching and native structured output capability

prompt caching on Bedrock is model-dependent and fails silently—when cache_read and cache_write are both zero despite input_tokens > 0, rebar must warn the operator to prevent hidden full-price billing on every call

temperature and other sampling parameters are fatal (ValidationException 400) on some Bedrock model IDs (e.g. us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7 rejects temperature), breaking rebar's Pass-2 deterministic re-verify steps, requiring per-model-id capability overrides since pydantic-ai's _drop_unsupported_sampling_settings exists only in anthropic.py not bedrock.py
the Bedrock builder must live in a new leaf module src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py to avoid breaching providers.py's signed 300-LOC hard cap (currently at 289 LOC)

a second, distinct _MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES table (keyed on exact model id, not predicate) must be applied after f184's profile-shaped _REBAR_OVERRIDES to record measured per-model API defects without widening the signed _REBAR_OVERRIDES predicate contract

caching on Bedrock requires exactly two cache keys for parity with the direct-Anthropic path: bedrock_cache_instructions and bedrock_cache_tool_definitions—bedrock_cache_messages must NOT be set to avoid making Bedrock cache more than Anthropic, which would be a new behavior requiring separate measurement and decision
